title: The effect of ChatGPT on students’ learning performance, learning perception, and higher-order thinking: insights from a meta-analysis
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether ChatGPT improves student learning and under what conditions its effects are strongest. The authors note that prior studies on ChatGPT in education have reported mixed results, ranging from positive effects on achievement and motivation to null or negative effects, which motivated a quantitative synthesis.

The study uses a meta-analysis of 51 quasi-experimental and experimental studies published between November 2022 and February 2025. The included studies cover primary, secondary, and college contexts, although nearly all moderator analyses were driven by secondary and college samples. Outcomes were grouped into three categories: learning performance, learning perception, and higher-order thinking. The paper also codes moderating variables including grade level, type of course, learning model, intervention duration, ChatGPT role, and application area.

The main finding is that ChatGPT has a large positive effect on learning performance and moderate positive effects on learning perception and higher-order thinking. Effects were strongest in skills/competencies courses, problem-based learning, and interventions lasting 4–8 weeks for performance; learning perception improved across durations, with larger effects after longer use; and higher-order thinking benefits were most pronounced when ChatGPT functioned as an intelligent tutor. The authors conclude that ChatGPT can support learning when embedded in structured pedagogical designs, but they also caution that future studies should better examine how it is used and for what learning purpose.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI chatbot / large language model system used for conversational text generation, tutoring, feedback, and related instructional tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: This meta-analysis examined ChatGPT as the intervention across experimental and quasi-experimental studies on student learning outcomes; the paper also discusses ChatGPT's role in education broadly, including tutoring, assessment, personalized recommendation, and learning support.

findings.finding_summary: Across 44 independent effects from 51 studies, ChatGPT had a large positive effect on learning performance (Hedges's g=0.867, 95% CI 0.683 to 1.052, p<0.001). The paper notes substantial heterogeneity (I2=89.243%) and reports stronger effects in problem-based learning and 4-8 week interventions.
findings.measure: Learning performance (tests/exams; standardized mean difference across experimental vs control groups)

findings.finding_summary: Across 19 independent effects, ChatGPT had a moderate positive effect on learning perception (Hedges's g=0.456, 95% CI 0.287 to 0.625, p<0.001). The paper reports that intervention duration moderated the effect, with longer interventions (>8 weeks) showing larger gains.

Across 9 independent effects, ChatGPT had a moderate positive effect on higher-order thinking (Hedges's g=0.457, 95% CI 0.255 to 0.650, p<0.001). The paper reports that ChatGPT was most effective when used as an intelligent tutor, and that effects varied by course type.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a meta-analysis of 51 experimental/quasi-experimental studies with quantified pooled effects and heterogeneity analyses. The review explicitly reports inclusion criteria, effect-size computation, and moderator analyses, which supports high evidence quality despite heterogeneity.
impact_tier_rationale: The pooled effects are medium to large by the paper's own conventions, including a large effect on learning performance (g=0.867) and moderate effects on learning perception and higher-order thinking (both g=0.456-0.457). These exceed the threshold for blue impact.
